name: Levofloxacin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Levofloxacin clearance falls and its half-life lengthens when creatinine clearance (CrCl) drops below 50 mL/min, so the US label extends the dosing interval. Neither hemodialysis nor continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD) removes it, so no supplemental doses are needed.

bands.recommendation: Usual dose: 250, 500 or 750 mg every 24 hours by infection (label).
CrCl ≥50: usual dose. CrCl 20–49: 750 mg every 48 hours; or 500 mg once, then 250 mg every 24 hours; 250 mg regimen unchanged (label).
CrCl 20–49: as above. CrCl 10–19: 750 mg once, then 500 mg every 48 hours; or 500 mg once, then 250 mg every 48 hours; 250 mg regimen becomes every 48 hours (no change for uncomplicated UTI) (label).
CrCl 10–19: as above. Below 10 not on dialysis: not addressed in label; specialist input.

hd: 750 mg once, then 500 mg every 48 hours; or 500 mg once, then 250 mg every 48 hours. No supplemental dose after dialysis. 250 mg regimen: no information (label).
pd: CAPD: same as hemodialysis; no supplemental dose (label).
crrt: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.
dialyzable: No: not efficiently removed by hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis (label).
monitoring: Tendon rupture, QT prolongation, dysglycemia, central nervous system effects; risk higher in older adults and kidney impairment.

pediatric.approved_ages: Inhalational anthrax (post-exposure) and plague: 6 months and older. Not established under 6 months; safety beyond 14 days not studied (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Tablet label: 50 kg or more, 500 mg every 24 hours; 30 kg to <50 kg, 250 mg every 12 hours. No mg/kg dose for children under 30 kg in this tablet label (see notes).

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney-dosing data in the US label; specialist (pediatric nephrology) input.

pediatric.notes: Quinolones cause arthropathy in juvenile animals (label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
